history.title: Teenager Patents World's First Synthetic Dye
history.desc: 18-year-old chemist William Henry Perkin patented mauveine, the first synthetic dye, discovered by accident while trying to synthesize malaria medicine. He built a factory and launched the modern chemical industry.
history.historicalQuote: Accidental discoveries mean nothing unless you have the vision to turn a lab mistake into a global market solution.
history.speaker: William Henry Perkin
history.takeaway: Great entrepreneurs recognize opportunity in accidental outcomes rather than throwing failed experiments away.

history.title: Birth of Karen Spärck Jones (Search Engine Pioneer)
history.desc: Computer scientist Karen Spärck Jones was born on this day. She created IDF (Inverse Document Frequency), the core statistical formula behind modern web search engines like Google.
history.historicalQuote: Computing is too important to be left to men. Words are the most complex form of data we have.
history.speaker: Karen Spärck Jones (Computer Scientist)
history.takeaway: Fundamental math formulas created decades ago power today's multi-trillion dollar search technologies.

history.title: First Audio Tape Recorder Used in Live Radio Broadcast
history.desc: New York radio station WQXR broadcasted live using a magnetic tape recorder for the first time, revolutionizing audio broadcasting and media distribution.
history.historicalQuote: Recorded media liberates broadcasting from the constraints of live execution.
history.speaker: WQXR Broadcast Announcement
history.takeaway: Time-shifting tech allows creators to build content once and scale distribution endlessly.

history.title: Birth of Lee de Forest (Inventor of Vacuum Tube)
history.desc: Inventor Lee de Forest was born. His invention of the Audion vacuum tube enabled sound amplification, making radio broadcasts, sound films, and early computers possible.
history.historicalQuote: I discovered an invisible empire of the air, and electronic amplification will build the modern world.
history.speaker: Lee de Forest
history.takeaway: Core hardware inventions unlock entirely new consumer media and computing industries.

history.title: Birth of Antoine Lavoisier (Father of Chemistry)
history.desc: Antoine Lavoisier was born on this day. He transformed chemistry from guesswork into a quantitative science, named Oxygen and Hydrogen, and stated the Law of Conservation of Mass.
history.historicalQuote: Nothing is lost, nothing is created, everything is transformed.
history.speaker: Antoine Lavoisier
history.takeaway: Rigorous measurement and data collection convert messy concepts into predictable market frameworks.

history.title: 19th Amendment Certified (Women's Equality Day)
history.desc: The 19th Amendment was officially certified on this day, granting women the right to vote in the U.S. and opening new horizons for female leadership and business ownership.
history.historicalQuote: The day will come when men will recognize women as their peers, not only at the fireside, but in the councils of the nation.
history.speaker: Susan B. Anthony
history.takeaway: Expanding workforce and civic participation drives exponential growth in innovation and enterprise.
